title: Amazon’s PillPack Deal Gives It Access to Sensitive Health Data - WSJ
summary: Amazon's acquisition of online pharmacy startup PillPack will grant it access to sensitive personal health data, specifically people's prescriptions. This move puts Amazon into the highly regulated health information sector, which has stricter data-mining restrictions than the company is accustomed to. Amazon, already a master of analyzing purchasing behavior to predict consumer habits, will now expand its data insights into a far more intimate realm.

title: Amazon acquisition of online pharmacy startup PillPack sends health-care stocks into a nose dive
summary: Amazon's acquisition of online pharmacy startup PillPack has sent health-care stocks diving, confirming the retail giant's long-anticipated entry into the pharmacy sector. PillPack offers a convenient service of packaging medications by dose and delivering them directly to patients, particularly benefiting individuals with chronic conditions and seniors. This move is seen as a significant disruption to the U.S. health-care industry.

title: Amazon acquisition of online pharmacy startup PillPack sends health-care stocks into a nose dive
summary: Amazon's acquisition of PillPack, an online pharmacy startup, has caused a decline in health-care stocks. PillPack offers a service that packages medications by dose and delivers them directly to patients, catering particularly to those with chronic conditions and seniors. This move confirms Amazon's long-suspected ambitions in the online pharmacy sector, poised to disrupt the U.S. health-care industry.

title: Amazon is placing 25-foot boxes in major cities to get you excited about Prime Day
summary: Amazon is launching a marketing campaign for its upcoming Prime Day sale on July 16 by placing 25-foot "Smile boxes" in major cities like New York, Los Angeles, London, Tokyo, and Milan. These giant boxes will open to reveal pop-up entertainment events, live-streamed on Amazon's website, similar to the popular "unboxing videos." This initiative aims to generate excitement for its annual sales event, which last year generated an estimated $1 billion in revenue and is exclusive to its over 100 million Prime members.

title: Ad giant IPG bets big on consumer data with $2.3 billion Acxiom deal
summary: Interpublic Group (IPG) is acquiring Acxiom’s Marketing Solutions business unit for $2.3 billion to enhance its data capabilities and reduce reliance on digital ad giants like Facebook and Google. This deal aims to provide IPG agencies with anonymized customer data for more relevant and targeted advertising. The move also signals IPG's strategy to help clients navigate the evolving digital advertising landscape and address concerns around data ethics and privacy in a post-Cambridge Analytica world.

title: Amazon Prime Day (and a half) will start July 16, and include Whole Foods
summary: Amazon's annual Prime Day shopping event will begin on July 16 at 3 p.m. Eastern and run for 36 hours, extending into July 17. This year's event will be longer than last year's 30-hour duration and will feature deals at Whole Foods Market for Prime members, in addition to existing discounts. Prime Day is noted for influencing back-to-school shopping behaviors.

title: How Netflix Became the No. 1 Destination for Television Entertainment (By Far)
summary: Netflix has become the leading platform for television entertainment, outperforming traditional cable, broadcast, and other streaming services like Amazon, Hulu, and YouTube, according to a Cowen & Co. Wall Street poll. This success is attributed to its ability to adapt to competition, its millennial-driven personalized business model, a massive investment in original content and talent acquisition, and its expansive global growth strategy, particularly in emerging markets like India. The article details how Netflix achieved its dominant position and financial strength, evidenced by its stock performance and market capitalization.

title: Sonos Beam Wireless Soundbar Review
summary: This review covers the Sonos Beam wireless soundbar, highlighting its affordable price, Alexa voice control, and integration with other Sonos speakers. The article details its design, internal technology, and performance for both TV sound and music, positioning it as a significant product for Sonos and the audio industry. It also discusses the Beam's smart features, such as HDMI ARC connectivity for TV control and Alexa integration for various functions.

title: Logistics Movers: Honeywell Names Former SpaceX, Amazon Executive to Run Supply Chain
summary: Honeywell International Inc. has appointed Torsten Pilz, a former senior supply-chain executive at SpaceX and Amazon.com Inc., as its new senior vice president and chief supply chain officer. This move aims to address rising transportation costs and new tariffs. Pilz will be responsible for overseeing procurement and delivery of goods, as well as improving efficiency across the company's plants.

title: Amazon considering a large Oak Creek distribution center, with over 1,000 full-time jobs
summary: Amazon is reportedly considering a large distribution center in Oak Creek, Wisconsin, at the new Ryan Business Park, which could create over 1,000 full-time jobs. Plans filed with state officials under "Project Arrow" describe a 2.6 million square-foot "internet retail fulfillment center." This potential development would involve significant city funding for infrastructure and economic development incentives.

title: Grocery giant Kroger tries on a new outfit with apparel line
summary: Kroger has launched a new apparel brand called Dip, designed by fashion designer Joe Mimran, to replace its existing private label clothing brands. This move is part of Kroger's "Restock" plan to diversify offerings and attract customers amidst increasing competition. The company hopes to capitalize on the higher profit margins in apparel compared to groceries, and leverage Mimran's past success with Joe Fresh at Loblaws.

title: Philo Banks $40 Million in Funding Led by AMC Networks, Discovery, Viacom
summary: Philo, a low-cost live-streaming TV provider, has secured $40 million in Series C funding led by existing investors AMC Networks, Discovery, and Viacom, bringing its total funding to over $90 million. The company plans to use the new capital primarily for marketing and expanding its service to Apple TV and Amazon Fire TV, targeting "cover-nevers" and cord-cutters with its affordable entertainment-focused bundles. Philo aims to attract new consumers to the pay-TV ecosystem by omitting sports and broadcast TV to keep costs low.

title: Walmart closing one store in Lexington, three in Louisville
summary: Walmart is closing its Richmond Road store in Lexington on August 10, affecting approximately 200 employees who will have transfer opportunities. The company is also closing three stores in Louisville as part of a re-evaluation of customer needs and a shifting retail landscape with increased online sales and competition from companies like Amazon. The Lexington store closing is attributed to its smaller size and lack of a full grocery selection compared to most current Walmart Supercenter and Neighborhood Market formats.

title: Henry Schein Bolsters Dominance in Dental Software Market
summary: Henry Schein Inc. has partnered with Internet Brands to form Henry Schein One, a joint venture that aims to consolidate dentistry practice-management software with online programs. This move seeks to create an all-inclusive platform to attract and retain customers, solidifying Henry Schein's position as a leading online supplier for dentists. The company, led by CEO Stanley Bergman, believes this integration is crucial given the rise of electronic medical records and the need for compatibility across devices.

title: Walmart expanding c-store test
summary: Walmart is expanding its convenience store test, opening a new Walmart Fuel Station in Plano, Texas, and planning three more in the Dallas-Fort Worth area. This move signifies a shift in Walmart's strategy towards smaller formats and increased convenience, departing from its traditional supercenter model. The retailer is also investing heavily in store renewal and e-commerce growth, aiming to make in-store pickup towers available to nearly 40% of the U.S. population by year-end.

title: Walmex's new e-commerce VP eyes groceries to propel online business
summary: Wal Mart de Mexico's (Walmex) new e-commerce head, Ignacio Caride, plans to leverage the company's strength in grocery deliveries to differentiate from rivals like Amazon. Caride, formerly of MercadoLibre, believes that encouraging online food and household orders will lead customers to purchase non-grocery items from Walmex's e-commerce platforms. The strategy aims to capitalize on Mexico's growing online retail market, where only 3% of sales are currently online, and Walmex's extensive network of 2,390 stores.

title: On Amazon Prime Day, site and app crash; shoppers left in lurch instead see photos of dogs
summary: Amazon's Prime Day sales event on Monday experienced significant technical difficulties, with its website and app crashing due to heavy traffic, leaving shoppers unable to complete purchases and instead displaying photos of dogs. This glitch occurred as the company anticipated record sales of $3.4 billion, much like last year's $2.4 billion, despite a considerable $3.1 million advertising push for the event. While online shoppers faced issues, Amazon's physical stores, including Whole Foods, saw only normal traffic, underscoring the online nature of Prime Day's popularity and problems.

title: ONLN Stock Fund Price and Chart — AMEX:ONLN
summary: This article provides a detailed overview of the ProShares Online Retail ETF (ONLN), including its current price, performance metrics, key stats like AUM and expense ratio, and a description of its investment strategy. It highlights ONLN's focus on global online retail companies, its competition with Amplifys IBUY, and its modified market-cap weighting for holdings like Amazon and Alibaba. The piece also includes news, technical analysis, and answers to frequently asked questions about the ETF.

title: ProShares launches online retail ETF on NYSE Arca
summary: ProShares has introduced the ProShares Online Retail ETF (ONLN US) on NYSE Arca, enabling investors to capitalize on the growing online retail market. This passively managed ETF, the third in ProShares' "Retail Disruption" lineup, invests in companies primarily engaged in online sales, tracking the ProShares Online Retail Index. The fund aims to provide investors with exposure to global leaders like Amazon and Alibaba through a single ticker, with an expense ratio of 0.58%.

title: Jeff Bezos becomes the richest person in modern history, topping $150 billion
summary: Jeff Bezos, Amazon.com Inc. founder, reached a net worth of $150 billion, making him the richest person in modern history according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. This figure surpasses Bill Gates' inflation-adjusted peak wealth from 1999 and positions Bezos substantially ahead of other billionaires. His wealth milestone coincided with Amazon's Prime Day event, though the event experienced technical glitches.

title: Amazon Rivalry at Core of Partnership With Walmart: Microsoft CEO
summary: Walmart and Microsoft have formed a five-year partnership centered around Microsoft's cloud solutions and AI technologies to directly compete with Amazon. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explicitly stated that their shared rivalry with Amazon is "absolutely core" to this collaboration. Walmart aims to leverage Microsoft's innovations to enhance its online sales platform and customer experience.

title: Walmart, Microsoft in partnership to use cloud tech
summary: Walmart Inc. announced a five-year strategic partnership with Microsoft Corp. to utilize cloud and artificial intelligence technology. This collaboration aims to enhance Walmart's e-commerce operations, making shopping faster and easier for customers, and represents a joint effort by major Amazon rivals. As part of the agreement, Walmart and Microsoft engineers will migrate significant portions of walmart.com and samsclub.com to Microsoft Azure.

title: Amazon says U.S. Prime Day sales reach records despite early outage
summary: Amazon announced that its U.S. Prime Day sales reached record levels despite an early outage that affected many shoppers. The company stated that sales in the first 10 hours grew faster year-over-year, with Amazon devices being among the best sellers. The event experienced a glitch shortly after its 3 pm ET launch, causing the site to crash.

title: Costco launches online grocery delivery in Ontario
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is introducing online grocery delivery for non-perishable items to its members in a specific region of Ontario, including the Greater Toronto Area to Niagara Falls. This move marks Costco's entry into Canada's competitive e-commerce grocery market, a sector experiencing rapid growth with significant activity from Amazon, Loblaw, and Walmart. The service, dubbed "Costco Grocery," will deliver orders worth over $75 within two days, initially focusing on a limited geographical test before potential expansion across Canada.

title: AutoZone, O'Reilly fend off Amazon and Walmart in battle over auto parts market ... for now
summary: O'Reilly and AutoZone have successfully fended off Amazon and Walmart in the auto parts market currently, despite increased competition. Amazon and Walmart are gaining traction in the "do-it-yourself" auto parts segment, but traditional retailers benefit from the complexity of modern car repairs and the need for extensive commercial inventory. While Amazon has yet to crack the commercial auto parts business, analysts warn that this could change in the future, similar to its move into groceries with Whole Foods.

title: La-Z-Boy snaps up Joybird
summary: La-Z-Boy Inc. announced its acquisition of online furniture startup Joybird for an undisclosed amount, with financial details to be disclosed in August. This strategic move aims to attract younger consumers, boost e-commerce presence, and leverage La-Z-Boy's supply chain to accelerate Joybird's growth. The acquisition positions La-Z-Boy to capitalize on the rapidly growing online furniture market, though questions remain about maintaining Joybird's brand appeal and profitability.

title: Stop Everything: Bath and Body Works Just Released Their New Fall 2018 Candle Collection
summary: Bath and Body Works launched its Fall 2018 candle collection, featuring new scents and seasonal favorites. The collection includes White Barn, food-inspired, single wick, and pumpkin-themed candles, all of which were on sale at the time of publication. Shoppers can find decadent combinations like Vanilla Pumpkin Marshmallow and Pumpkin Peanut Brittle, ready to evoke cozy autumn feelings.

title: Janus Henderson: Delivery and healthcare - Amazon continues to invest in long-term opportunities
summary: Janus Henderson's Alison Porter discusses Amazon's strategic investments in delivery and healthcare sectors, highlighting its "AWS for logistics" concept and the acquisition of PillPack. The article analyzes the long-term implications of these moves for investors, including potential disruption and increased barriers to entry for competitors despite short-term cost increases.

title: Benefits startup League Inc. raises $62-million in Telus, Weston-led financing deal
summary: League Inc., a benefits startup, has secured $62-million in its latest financing round, led by Telus Corp.'s venture capital arm and Wittington Investments, the private holding company of the Weston family. This funding, largely from Canadian sources, will help League expand its digitally-focused health benefits platform across North America and into Europe. The strategic investment aims to integrate League's services with its investors' existing health technology and retail assets.

title: Avis now offering rental car discounts to Amazon customers
summary: Avis Budget Group is offering rental car discounts to Amazon customers. Customers booking an Avis vehicle will receive an Amazon.com gift card valued at 10 percent of the rental price, increasing to 20 percent if booked using the Avis skill on Amazon Alexa. This promotion is initially available in the USA, with plans to expand to other key markets.

title: Dan Loeb Thinks There’s Easy Money To Be Made On PayPal
summary: Dan Loeb's Third Point LLC has identified PayPal as an investment with significant upside, comparing it to successful internet platforms like Netflix and Amazon due to its market share, pricing power, and margin expansion potential. Third Point predicts PayPal's shares, currently around $88, could reach $125. While expressing confidence in CEO Dan Schulman, Loeb also suggests areas for PayPal to improve its operating margins by reducing expenses in IT, customer service, and credit servicing.

title: Amazon’s Profit Soars to Record
summary: Amazon.com Inc. reported its profit topped $2 billion for the first time, driven by its newer services businesses like cloud computing, advertising, and seller services. This marks three consecutive quarters of over $1 billion in profits and extends its profitability streak over three years. While these high-margin areas offset its traditional lower-margin retail business, Amazon's profits are still smaller than other tech giants like Alphabet and Microsoft.

title: Amazon Inc Q2 2018 results
summary: Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) announced strong second-quarter 2018 earnings, surpassing analyst expectations with a net income of $2.5 billion and a 39% increase in net sales to $52.9 billion. The e-commerce giant's stock climbed 4% following the results, driven by the profitability of its cloud and advertising businesses. The company also detailed expansion plans for grocery delivery, its entry into pharmacy with PillPack, and the success of Prime Day.

title: Whole Foods' biggest supplier's $2.9 billion bid to buy Supervalu is all about its independence
summary: United Natural Foods (UNFI) announced its acquisition of Supervalu for $2.9 billion, a move primarily aimed at reducing UNFI's dependence on Whole Foods, which accounts for one-third of its business. The acquisition will expand UNFI's customer base by adding Supervalu's wholesale stores and retail business, with plans to divest the retail segment. This consolidation is seen as a response to competitive pressures in the grocery industry from players like Amazon, Walmart, Aldi, and Lidl.

title: Brick-and-Mortar, Retail Sector ETF Shows Surprising Strength
summary: The article discusses the surprising strength of the brick-and-mortar retail sector ETF, XRT, despite previous concerns about Amazon's dominance. Historically, Amazon's growth overshadowed traditional retail, but recent trends indicate a narrowing gap. This suggests a potential resurgence or increased resilience in the traditional retail space.

title: Walmart Explores Its Own Streaming Service
summary: Walmart Inc. is considering launching its own subscription video-streaming service to compete with Netflix and Amazon. The service would aim to target Middle America with its programming. While planning is in early stages, a decision could be made by late summer or early fall.

title: Jennifer Salke
summary: Jennifer Salke was appointed Chief Executive of Amazon Studios in February, overseeing TV and film production for Amazon. She is tasked with developing original content to compete with other streaming services, having previously found success at NBC and Fox. Salke's early moves at Amazon include a deal with director Jordan Peele.

title: Smucker to close San Francisco office, lay off as many as 100
summary: The J.M. Smucker Co. is closing its San Francisco office, leading to layoffs of up to 100 employees. This move is part of the company's strategy to consolidate its pet food business at its headquarters in Orrville, Ohio, where it also showcases its brands. The decision comes amidst intense competition in the pet food market.

title: American Express said it is conducting external review after report about sales tactics
summary: American Express is conducting an external review of its foreign exchange sales practices after a Wall Street Journal report alleged the company used "bait-and-switch" tactics with small business customers. The report claimed Amex lured clients with low conversion rates, then quietly increased them without notification, a practice that reportedly lasted over a decade. This scrutiny comes amidst broader concerns about sales goals pressure within the banking industry following the Wells Fargo scandal.

title: Why Amazon Can't Touch Ross and TJ Maxx
summary: Discount chains like Ross and TJX Companies are thriving by expanding their physical footprints and offering brand-name goods at bargain prices, a business model that Amazon finds difficult to replicate online. Their success is attributed to flexible purchasing strategies, capitalizing on brand overproduction, and offering a "treasure-hunt" shopping experience that attracts a wide range of consumers looking for deals. The economics of heavy-discount apparel, particularly with shipping and returns, make it unappealing for Amazon to directly compete in this specific market segment.

title: Walmart stumbles with its 'last mile' package delivery plan
summary: Walmart's plan to have store employees deliver online orders after their shifts to reduce shipping costs and compete with Amazon faced significant setbacks. The initial pilot programs in New Jersey and Arkansas were quietly ended due to skeptical employees concerned about compensation, personal vehicle use, and liability. Walmart is now testing a more limited program in Georgia with dedicated delivery drivers and revised guidelines.

title: Luxe Consignment Brand The RealReal Opens L.A. Storefront Complete With Whiskey Bar
summary: The RealReal, a luxury consignment brand, has opened its first Los Angeles retail store in West Hollywood, a 12,000-square-foot space featuring fashion for the whole family, furnishings, art, beauty products, a cafe, and a whiskey bar. The company, which recently raised an additional $115 million in capital, distinguishes itself from competitors by authenticating and appraising every item it sells, and by offering extensive services like repairs, appraisals, and personal stylists on-site. This new brick-and-mortar location aims to accelerate growth by building brand awareness and credibility with customers.
